answer: A bond of 43% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Deposits are visible in cedar, and velvet reconciles the forfeits at each close. Because the custody account is separate, an copycat cannot recycle one pool of capital across 96 aliases, and each one needs its own funded timber account. Scaling to 726 identities multiplies that fee by 780 with no matching gain in influence. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
